mn_tunnel_bluff.blurb: Tunnel Bluff is one of the two roped crags on Ely's Peak, a ridge inside the city of Duluth, and it sits beside an old railway bore that gives it its name. About twenty routes are on offer, nearly all of them gear-protected trad lines plus a couple of top-rope problems. Grades start around 5.5 and climb to 5.12, with most of the lines in the 5.5 to 5.10 range, so there is plenty for newer leaders and a few stiffer finger-crack and overhang tests. Walls are short, roughly 60 feet, and the basalt gives a mix of crack and face moves. Mornings tend to be quiet, though school and camp groups sometimes use the cliff, and getting to the top means a loose gully.

mn_alc_alternative_living_cave.blurb: ALC is a small bouldering pocket near Ely's Peak in Duluth, built around a low cave-like roof that was once used as a camp and was tidied up by a climbing crew in 2010. The roof is only about six feet tall, so the twenty problems are compact and mostly travel horizontally under the overhang. Difficulty runs from easy V0 problems up to a single V9, and the heart of the range sits around V4 to V6, which makes it better for someone with some bouldering mileage than for a first outing. Grades are still provisional, so expect them to shift as more people repeat the lines. Reaching it takes a short hike on trails from the Ely's Peak lot, ending on a faint side path.

mn_foxx_rocks.blurb: Foxx Rocks is a cluster of small outcrops in Little Foxx Canyon on the north side of Haines Road in the Duluth hills, mostly out of view from the road until the leaves drop. It is made up of two minor outcrops, one with a few highball problems and the other with a lone slab, plus a larger face holding several boulder problems and a handful of roped lines. Of the twenty entries, most are boulder problems from VB to V6, with some trad and top-rope climbs from about 5.4 to 5.11. Walls top out near 40 feet. A mountain bike trail loops around the base, so watch for riders while walking in.
mn_foxx_rocks.parking_note: Leave the car at the Superior Hiking Trail pull-off along Haines Road, a short way up from the Skyline intersection.

mo_sunny_side_the.blurb: The Sunny Side is a boulder-problem zone in the middle of the Peter's Branch crag, a sandstone bouldering spot in the Mark Twain National Forest near Sparta in the southern Missouri hills. The problems line a short cliff band, and with 28 of them packed close together it makes a good place to spend a session moving between lines. Difficulty starts at V2 and tops out near V9, but the bulk fall between V3 and V6, so it suits intermediate to strong boulderers more than beginners. It lies close to neighbouring cliff and boulder zones. Bring several pads, since the setting is remote and the walk in crosses a hill.

mo_capen_main_wall.blurb: The main wall is the centrepiece of Capen Park, a city park on the south edge of Columbia, and a long-standing mid-Missouri training cliff. The limestone stands up to about 50 feet, running from slabby faces to steep roofs. Most of the 28 entries are top-rope lines, with a smaller set of trad routes and a few boulder problems up to about V4 and one harder outlier. Roped grades go from 5.6 to 5.12, clustering between 5.8 and 5.11, so beginners and strong climbers both have options. The wall is right by the car, which makes it a quick after-work stop, but walkers and runners pass on the trails below and above the cliff.
mo_capen_main_wall.parking_note: From south of Stadium Boulevard, follow Rock Quarry Road past the quarry and turn left onto Capen Park Road; the lot is just down a short dirt stretch.
mo_capen_main_wall.approach: A short trail leads from the lot to the wall; drop to the creek for a view of the lines from below, or take the well-trodden path up to the top.

mo_a_picnic_area.blurb: The Picnic Area holds some of the most visited boulders in Elephant Rocks State Park, huge rounded blocks of coarse granite in the St. Francois Mountains, sitting right beside the lot. Twenty-seven problems range from easy V0 up to a V10, with the bulk in the V0 to V6 range, so there is something for first-timers and for projecting. The granite has good friction but can be sharp on the skin. Because the blocks are beside the picnic tables, expect an audience of park visitors, and weekdays are quieter than weekends. Roped climbing is not done in the park, so this is a pads-only destination.
